integrity.anchor_registry_note: The corpus provenance gate verifies each anchor against the file that anchor names and stores no registry-level digest of its own. This digest is recorded so a signature also pins which anchor set was in force.
integrity.verbatim_block_note: The block in section 3 is the file's decoded text with any single trailing newline removed, which is what the markdown fences require. `record_sha256` above is over the raw file bytes and is the digest a signature refers to; this one is over the text as embedded, so a verifier can compare either.

value: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session (opencode). The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime. No platform-issued session id was available to the reviewer, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. This is an AUTOMATED REVIEW: it is NOT organizational independence, NOT human confirmation and NOT a qualified-checker result. No human reviewer, no independent party and no separate agent session participated. Consistent with corpus-policy.json#/review_policy/ai_review_limitations, a distinct agent session would not have been independence either.
Automated review in one session. Not organizational independence, not human confirmation, not a qualified-checker result.
human_approval_status is 'pending' for every record covered. No human reviewer signed any of them, and this review is not a signature.
No record covered carries production authority or product verification credit.

PARTIAL SCOPE, AND THE PART NOT COVERED IS THE LARGER PART. This review covers the uncovered implementation group in one profile only. The uncovered population is 110 identifiers and the largest groups in it are NOT implementation: 35 finding records, 18 scenario records and 18 review records. Those were NOT reached. A finding record is itself review output, so reviewing them is a meta-review and is arguably higher-value than reviewing implementation records; it was not done here because reading 35 records of roughly 12.7 kB each was not affordable in this pass, and a review that certifies without reading would be worse than no review. The group chosen was the largest one that could be read in full AND that the profile-split requirement actually bites on. That is a statement about budget, not a judgement that the unreviewed groups are in better shape.
No implementation record was edited, revised or re-hashed by this review. The three findings are dispositions for the owner; every stored review digest over the reviewed records still verifies.

dispositions.action: Accepted. Three small reconciliations, all on one record and none of them touching engineering content: (1) change code_locations[4].symbol_role from 'definition' to whatever is true of lines 234-239 - a configuration block inside the function - or drop the location, since anchor FB2-SRC-COD-000078 already records the range; (2) qualify evidence_status.method's 'each named symbol was confirmed to occur inside its recorded line_range' so it does not assert a check that this location fails and the following limitation already contradicts; (3) make verified_against_pinned_source mean one thing - either split it into the four checks it stands for or rename it so it does not read as a summary of all four (see FB2-REV-FND-000173). Referred to the implementation and traceability owners. This review changed nothing: any edit to an implementation record changes its content digest and invalidates every stored review digest that covers it, so the repair is a revision with re-derived digests and belongs to the owner.

Accepted, and now half-closed by the owner. The disposition named two options - give every behaviour a file or anchor reference, or declare that behaviour evidence resolves against the record's code_locations and machine-check it. The second was taken, and the first was not, with the reason now on the record: a path added to 84 behaviours across 14 records is an assertion, while resolution against a located symbol whose pinned blob is re-derived is a verification, and the schema and three validator rules now say so. Of the 17 behaviours this review counted as unresolvable at the time, 16 are contained citations and were never wrong; the 17th was wrong in the sense that mattered - unattributable - and is repaired. WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and is not claimed closed here: no behaviour names a file, so a citation whose symbol happens to be the wrong located symbol would still resolve; and the control reports pinned bytes as unverifiable rather than failing when a checkout cannot produce them. Referred to the implementation owner for the first and to the toolchain owner for the second.

Accepted, and closed by the owner. Both options the finding named - split the flag or rename it - were superseded by a third that is stronger than either: split it into the four named checks, keep the aggregate as an explicitly derived conjunction, and make BOTH machine-checked (one rule for the aggregate contradicting its parts, one for a part disagreeing with the pinned blob). A rename would have left four checks behind a name a reader had to look up; a split alone would have left four asserted booleans in place of one, which is a worse record than the one it replaced. The migration touched all 14 records and the 31 link endpoints that name them; every link's recorded endpoint revision was advanced with the refresh recorded in its own provenance_repair block, following the pattern the 2026-10-01 link-endpoint revision repair established, and the derived change_suspect_status of those 31 links is now true, which is the honest derived value: they were authored against revision 1 and no re-examination of them is recorded. The two review records covering these fourteen re-derived their digests, which is a digest re-derivation and not a re-review. FB2-REV-FND-000171 item (2) was actioned because the split made it unavoidable; item (1) remains open and is referred to the implementation owner.

Accepted, and referred rather than actioned. Two changes were made available to this review and neither was taken. Re-deriving the 13 hashes against the pinned blob would make every one of them contradict the hash_note that explains the re-recording, and the hash_note is the disclosure that makes the divergence honest rather than hidden; replacing it with a bare pinned hash would trade an accurate note for a consistent field and lose the reader's ability to know the hash moved. Advancing each anchor's commit to the commit that actually holds the recorded bytes would resolve the inconsistency, but deciding which commit an anchor MEANS is a source-registry decision and the registry is owned by the digest workstream. What this review did instead is make the shape visible: the new pinned-blob reader reports its resolution source for every citation and every code location, so the same question can now be asked of the anchors without re-inventing the measurement. The honest position today is that the corpus asserts nothing about whether an anchor's hash matches its own commit, and this finding says so.

findings.description: Two fields on the as_is EMAC driver record over-claim, and both concern its fifth code_location. The location itself is NOT a defect and this review says so first: evidence_status.limitations[0] already discloses that EMAC_InitializeHardware's range 234-239 is 'the destination-address match configuration inside that function's body', that it duplicates the range anchor FB2-SRC-COD-000078 records, and that the anchor's own spelling 'EMAC_Initialize' names no symbol that exists in emac.c. That disclosure is accurate and I confirmed it against the pinned file. What is NOT accurate is everything around it. (1) code_locations[4] carries symbol_role 'definition' while the record's own limitation says the range is a block INSIDE the function body; the definition is at line 217 and is already listed as code_locations[0]. The field states something the same record contradicts one screen away. (2) evidence_status.method states 'Each named symbol was confirmed to occur inside its recorded line_range at the pin'. For this one location that check FAILS - EMAC_InitializeHardware does not occur anywhere in lines 234-239 - and the method sentence is not qualified by the limitation that follows it, so the method and the limitation disagree about whether the check was done. (3) The location is marked verified_against_pinned_source: true, which is true of three of the four checks the flag stands for (file exists, content_hash correct, range in bounds - all three independently re-derived and all three hold) and false of the fourth. A reader who audits provenance by reading the method and then trusting the flag would be told a check passed that the method, run, would have failed. NOT CLAIMED: no engineering content is wrong, no symbol is attributed to the wrong file, no hash is wrong, no anchor is wrong, and no safety-relevant statement depends on any of it. Two defects, both in the provenance bookkeeping of one record, and both of the 'reads stronger than it is' kind rather than the 'is false' kind.
findings.evidence: src/app/driver/emac/emac.c read with 'git show 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437:src/app/driver/emac/emac.c'. Line 217 is 'extern EMAC_RETURN_TYPE_e EMAC_InitializeHardware(uint8_t const *pEmacAddress) {'; lines 234-239 are the MAC-address configuration block inside it and contain no occurrence of the symbol. The record's code_locations[4] is {path: src/app/driver/emac/emac.c, symbol: EMAC_InitializeHardware, line_range: 234-239, symbol_role: definition, verified_against_pinned_source: true}. Independently recomputed: the file's sha256 at the pin equals the recorded content_hash and the file is 699 lines, so three of the four checks hold; the symbol-in-range check does not. The record's own evidence_status.limitations[0] discloses the range and the anchor duplication; the symbol_role field and the method sentence are not reconciled with it. Across the whole group, 80 of the other 81 code_locations do satisfy the symbol-in-range check. This review changed nothing.

findings.description: Behaviour evidence across this whole group was not self-attributing and was not covered by any automated control, and THAT HALF IS NOW CLOSED. All 14 implementation records and all 84 of their behaviours still cite an evidence_symbol and an evidence_line_range and no file, so the self-attribution gap is unchanged and is stated again here rather than declared fixed. What has changed is that the suite now READS behaviours[]. The implementation schema declares the resolution contract and three new provenance rules enforce it: behaviour_citation_unresolved, behaviour_citation_line_range_out_of_bounds and behaviour_citation_symbol_missing, run inside the provenance pass on every validate, every check and every mutation-scenario detector pass. RESOLUTION as the new control defines it: a behaviour citing (symbol S, range R) resolves when some code_location in the SAME record names S and its own range contains R; the resolved citation is then checked against the PINNED BLOB that code_location names, so the cited lines must be inside that blob and the resolved symbol must occur inside the code_location's range in it. This review's second option was taken and its first was not, and the reason is that resolution against the record's own located symbols is a stronger statement than a path that is only asserted. MEASURED BY THE NEW CONTROL, on the tree as this pass left it: 84 of 84 behaviours resolve - 68 to a code_location at exactly the cited range and 16 to one whose range CONTAINS the cited range - and all 84 were then checked against the pinned blob with 0 out-of-bounds and 0 absent symbols. THE 17 THIS REVIEW ORIGINALLY COUNTED ARE ACCOUNTED FOR: 16 of them are contained citations and are NOT defects. A behaviour citing lines 445-460 of a function the record locates as 415-508 is a pointer at a block inside a located function, which is the ordinary way to be more precise than the record's granularity, and the symbol matches the located symbol in every one of the 16. The 17th, AFE-IMP-PUBLISH, WAS A REAL DEFECT AND IS REPAIRED: it cited evidence_symbol DATA_WRITE_DATA at line 653 with no file, no code_location in that record named that symbol, and line 653 falls outside every code_location range the record carries (the nearest is LTC_Trigger at 833). Read at the pin, ltc_6813-1.c:653 is 'DATA_WRITE_DATA(ltc_state->ltcData.cellVoltage);' inside LTC_SaveVoltages, so the citation was accurate and merely unattributable; the implementation schema had no symbol_role for a call site, which is why the record had nowhere to put it, so 'macro_invocation' was added to the enum and the location recorded. The behaviour's own evidence_symbol and evidence_line_range are unchanged. RESIDUAL LIMIT, and it is a real one: no behaviour names a file, so resolution is containment within a located symbol and is only as strong as that symbol being the right one; and the pinned-blob check reports an UNVERIFIABLE class rather than passing when a checkout cannot produce the pinned bytes, which on a checkout with no git object store is the case for every location in a file that has changed since the pin.
findings.evidence: This review's original hand resolution of all 84 behaviours is unchanged and every one of its worked instances still holds. The new control re-derived the same set mechanically and agrees with this review on all 84, including the classification of the 17: 16 contained, 1 unresolved. The 1 was repaired as described and the control now reports 0 unresolved. The control's per-class tally is printed by 'corpus.py validate' and 'corpus.py check' under 'behaviour citations', including the number whose pinned bytes could not be produced in the current checkout; on a checkout with a git object store that number is 0, and in a 'git archive' of HEAD it is 19 because three files (soa.c, rtc.c, diag.c) carry implementation locations whose pinned bytes the archive does not contain. That 20 is reported as unverifiable and is neither a pass nor a failure. This review changed nothing about the 84 behaviour citations; it changed one record's code_locations and one record's evidence_status.method sentence.

findings.description: verified_against_pinned_source was a single boolean standing in for four separate checks, and at least one location in this group would fail one of them. ITS FOUR CONSTITUENTS: the file exists at the pinned commit; the recorded content_hash equals that pinned blob's sha256; the line_range lies within the file; and the symbol occurs inside the range. THE SPLIT IS NOW DONE and the four are named fields rather than a convention: pinned_file_exists, pinned_content_hash_matches, line_range_within_file and symbol_within_line_range. Every one of the 82 code_locations across the 14 records now carries all four, the aggregate remains as verified_against_pinned_source but is documented as the conjunction and nothing more, and each record's revision history preserves the previous per-location value under pinned_source_migration. The four are no longer merely split: a new rule, pinned_verification_aggregate_contradicts_parts, rejects a location that claims the aggregate while any part is false or undeclared, and a second rule, code_location_pinned_part_mismatch, re-derives all four from the pinned blob on every run and rejects a recorded value that does not match the derivation - so the parts are machine-checked rather than asserted, which splitting alone would not have achieved. MEASURED: 82 of 82 locations, 328 of 328 part declarations present, 328 of 328 agree with the derivation. THE ONE FAILURE THIS FINDING PREDICTED IS NOW VISIBLE AS DATA: src/app/driver/emac/emac.c:234-239 records symbol_within_line_range=false and therefore verified_against_pinned_source=false, where it previously recorded true. Before this pass 80 of 81 symbols occurred in their range and 81 of 81 aggregates said true; there are now 82 locations because the AFE repair added one, and the other 81 all still pass all four. So the flag was wrong exactly once and is now wrong in the same place for a reason a reader can see. ONE CONSEQUENCE WAS NOT ANTICIPATED and is recorded here: that location's own record asserted in evidence_status.method that every named symbol was confirmed to occur inside its recorded line_range, so recording the false part would have left the record contradicting itself. That sentence was qualified - which is item (2) of FB2-REV-FND-000171 and is the only part of 171 actioned here. Item (1) of 171, the symbol_role of that location, is NOT actioned and remains open. THIS WAS A NAMING AND GRANULARITY DEFECT, NOT A PROVENANCE FAILURE, and it still is one: nothing here says a location is wrong; it says the summary field was coarser than the method that produced it.
findings.evidence: Re-derived all four constituents for all 82 code_locations from 'git show 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437:<path>' rather than from the working tree, and the distinction matters: 14 of the 82 record the pinned blob's hash and have since changed in the working tree (soa.c, rtc.c, diag.c), so a working-tree reader would have reported 14 mismatches that are not defects. 82 of 82 files exist at the pin, 82 of 82 content hashes are correct, 82 of 82 ranges are in bounds, 81 of 82 symbols occur in their range. The single exception is the location FB2-REV-FND-000171 is about, and it is now recorded as such instead of being rounded up into a true aggregate. The previous per-location value is preserved in each record's revision_history.pinned_source_migration.previous_aggregate_per_location.

findings.description: Building the behaviour-citation control for FB2-REV-FND-000172 required resolving each citation against the PINNED BLOB rather than the checked-out file, and doing so exposed a defect class this corpus's only provenance reader cannot see. The corpus reads blobs with _file_sha256, which hashes the working tree, while every code_location and every source anchor names a COMMIT. Those are different questions and the corpus was only ever asking the second one in the first one's words: 'does this hash match the tree?' MEASURED on this tree: 13 of the 117 source anchors carrying a usable content_hash record a hash that is NOT the sha256 of the blob at the commit the SAME anchor names, and all 13 do match the checked-out file. The seven files are src/app/application/soa/soa.c (FB2-SRC-COD-000004, -000005, -000006, -000099), src/app/engine/diag/diag.c (-000009), src/app/engine/database/database.c (-000028, -000106), src/app/driver/rtc/rtc.c (-000044, -000045), src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c (-000071, -000095), src/app/engine/database/database.h (-000105) and src/app/engine/diag/diag.h (-000107). Each of the 13 carries a top-level hash_note saying the hash was re-recorded after a later fix, so the re-recording is DISCLOSED in prose; what is not true is the field. An anchor that says 'at commit 308028fb' and carries the hash of bytes that do not exist at 308028fb is internally inconsistent, and a reader who trusts the commit has no way to know the hash moved. THE IMPLEMENTATION RECORDS DISAGREE WITH THE REGISTRY ABOUT THESE FILES, and the implementation records are the consistent side: the code_locations in FB2-SW-IMP-000002 and -000007 record the pinned-blob hash for soa.c, rtc.c and diag.c and all 82 of them re-derive correctly. So the defect is in the source registry, not in the records this review covers. NOT REPAIRED HERE, deliberately: re-deriving those 13 hashes to the pinned blobs would contradict the hash_note that explains why they were re-recorded, and re-deriving them to whatever commit actually holds them is a provenance decision about which commit an anchor means - a question for the digest workstream that owns the registry, not for a review of implementation records. NOT A VALIDATION FAILURE either, because nothing in the corpus asserts the property; the corpus today asserts nothing about it, which is the finding.
findings.evidence: For every anchor with a usable content_hash, recomputed sha256 over 'git show <location.commit>:<location.path>' and compared with the recorded hash, and separately compared with sha256 of the checked-out file. 13 anchors diverge from the pinned blob; 13 of 13 match the working tree; 104 of 104 agree with the pinned blob. Also re-derived all 82 code_location content_hashes the same way: 82 of 82 agree with the pinned blob, and 14 of them disagree with the checked-out file, which is the number that shows why the working tree cannot stand in for the pin. The behaviour-citation control reports its pinned-blob resolution source per citation, so this divergence is now visible on every run for the code_location side and NOT for the anchor side - the anchor reader still hashes the working tree. That asymmetry is why this is recorded rather than fixed.

results_summary.findings_corrected_note: FB2-REV-FND-000171 was first written at medium severity and asserted that the duplicate location was UNDISCLOSED and cited by no behaviour. A second read of the same record found evidence_status.limitations[0] already discloses the range and the anchor duplication. The finding was REWRITTEN, not dropped and not softened into nothing: what survives is that symbol_role 'definition' contradicts the record's own limitation, that evidence_status.method's symbol-in-range sentence is not qualified by that limitation and is false for this location, and that verified_against_pinned_source is therefore true of three of its four constituents. Severity moved medium to low because the location is disclosed rather than hidden. Recorded here because a review that over-claims is the same defect as a review that under-claims, and because a reader comparing this record with the corpus's own disclosure should be able to see that the discrepancy was found and corrected rather than never noticed.
results_summary.statement: This revision added no review coverage. The fourteen implementation records this review covers were revised by the owner to act on two of this review's own findings, and this review has not read revision 2 of them. What changed here is the machine layer: the behaviour layer of every implementation record is now read by the suite, the four checks behind verified_against_pinned_source are now named fields that are re-derived from the pinned blob on every run, and one attribution defect this review could only report by hand is repaired. Coverage went up by the number of behaviours and code locations a control now verifies, and by nothing else. Every substantive finding this review raised is unchanged.

record_verbatim.review_method: The records were READ, not sampled, and the two claims that are machine-checkable were re-derived rather than accepted. (1) Every one of the 81 code_locations across the 14 records was checked against the PINNED source with 'git show 308028fb:<path>': file existence, the recorded content_hash recomputed from that pinned blob, the recorded line_range for in-bounds-ness, and whether the recorded symbol occurs inside that range. (2) Every absence claim the four synthetic records make was re-tested by searching the named file at the pinned commit for the tokens they say return nothing. (3) Every one of the 84 behaviours was resolved by hand to a file and a line range at the pinned commit, because no automated control in the suite verifies behaviour evidence. (4) The configuration claim FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 (as_is) rests on was checked against src/app/engine/config/diag_cfg.c at the pin. (5) requirement_gap_reason's intended meaning was established by reading how the records that carry it use it, BEFORE reporting anything about the seven that do not.

reviewer_identity.note: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session (opencode). The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime. No platform-issued session id was available to the reviewer, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. This is an AUTOMATED REVIEW: it is NOT organizational independence, NOT human confirmation and NOT a qualified-checker result. No human reviewer, no independent party and no separate agent session participated. Consistent with corpus-policy.json#/review_policy/ai_review_limitations, a distinct agent session would not have been independence either.

The fourteen implementation records this review covers were revised by the owner to act on FB2-REV-FND-000172 and FB2-REV-FND-000173: verified_against_pinned_source was split into the four checks it stood for, the aggregate was corrected on the one location that does not pass all four, the AFE record gained the code location its AFE-IMP-PUBLISH citation resolves to, and the EMAC record's own evidence_status.method sentence was qualified. NO ENGINEERING CONTENT CHANGED - no path, symbol, line range, content hash, symbol role, behaviour or description was altered, and every finding this review raised about those records is unchanged and still describes them. The digests recorded in reviewed_ids were re-derived against the revised records, so they now describe revision 2 of each. THAT IS A DIGEST RE-DERIVATION AND NOT A RE-REVIEW: this review has not read revision 2, and every claim below about the reviewed content rests on revision 1. The reviewed_ids revision fields were advanced to 2 for the same reason and with the same limit.

record_verbatim.scope: TARGETED SCOPE, AND THE TARGETING IS THE FINDING. The scope is the UNCOVERED IMPLEMENTATION GROUP and nothing else: every implementation record in the corpus that automated_review_coverage did not already cover. That is 10 identifiers in as_is and 4 identifiers in synthetic_reference, over 14 (profile, id) records. PROFILE-SCOPED, DELIBERATELY: under ID-RULE-004-A1 the pair (profile, id) is the key, and four identifiers (FB2-SW-IMP-000001, -000002, -000003, -000004) are carried by two records each. A review record carries one profile, so a single review cannot name both copies of one identifier without either duplicating an id into a profile it does not belong to, or asserting that one copy's content speaks for the other. Per FB2-REV-FND-000046 a profile-scoped review cannot cover both profiles' records under a shared id, so this group is split into two review records, one per profile. Coverage of the OTHER 96 uncovered identifiers (35 finding, 18 scenario, 18 review and the remaining implementation-related records, plus one-off families) is NOT claimed here and is named in limitations.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-REV-000019` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. NEVER record the approval in revision_history - doing so stales every link pinning this revision and invalidates every stored review digest. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
